newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, soyoil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, soyoil lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mostly higher on Friday, led by nearbys on strong commercial buying and firm cash basis levels, pit sources said.
Soyoil ended lower, weighed down by a larger-than-expected weekly crush figure.
The weekly National Oilseeds Processors Association crush report early Friday showed the U.S. soybean crush during the week ended July 23 at 23.891 million bushels.
Traders said the crush figure weighed on soyoil more than soymeal because there are already large stockpiles of soyoil while soymeal continues to be in demand.
There was continued talk of China cancelling South American soymeal purchases. Hong Kong traders said China had likely defaulted on soymeal cargoes but specific amounts were difficult to pinpoint.

Weather drew mixed reviews. Meteorologists predicted a hot weekend for the U.S. Midwest, followed by cooler temperatures and a chance for showers on Monday. But forecasters disagreed on rainfall amounts and coverage.
Soymeal ended $3.20 per ton higher to $0.50 lower with August up $3.20 at $252.20. Soyoil closed down 0.22 to 0.12 cent per lb with August down 0.22 at 21.42.

On the day, Cargill Inc was the key buyer of August soymeal, accounting for 500 lots, traders said. Smith Barney bought 300 August while Term Commodities and Prudential Securities each bought 300 December.
In soyoil, ADM sold 500 September while Produce Grain, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer and Merrill Lynch each sold 200 December.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 21,434 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,500 lots, against Wednesday's 10,932.
